page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-72-lssd is an arm64-based virtual server designed for memory-dense and I/O-intensive enterprise workloads. The instance is provisioned with 72 dedicated vCPUs operating on 64-bit ARM architecture without hardware multithreading. System memory is configured at 576 GB, maintaining an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it within a memory-optimized operating profile.

Storage architecture features an integrated array composed of 16 local NVMe SSD drives that provide a cumulative capacity of 6,442 GB. This direct-attached NVMe configuration provides localized low-latency data access and sustained input/output operations directly on the host. Hardware GPU accelerators are not present on this machine type, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Because the server relies on an arm64 processor design, software workloads must be compatible with or compiled for ARM to execute natively. The dense allocation of 72 dedicated cores paired with substantial memory and multi-terabyte NVMe storage yields high resource density and operational efficiency for scaled computing tasks. This configuration aligns with in-memory caching engines, transactional relational or NoSQL database clusters, and low-latency data ingestion pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-72-lssd is a high-memory compute instance powered by an arm64 processor architecture. The configuration includes 72 dedicated vCPUs paired with 576 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features 6,442 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD capacity across 16 drives, providing high-throughput local disk operations. The server does not include GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By leveraging arm64 architecture with dedicated core allocations, the platform provides resource density and consistent multi-threaded execution without multithreading contention. The combination of high RAM capacity, high core counts, and massive local NVMe disk arrays makes this instance well matched for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale transactional workloads, and localized big data processing.
